page: Microsoft Azure E16s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, provisioned with 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. Architectural CPU flags include AVX-512 extensions (avx512f, avx512_vnni), hardware-accelerated encryption via AES-NI and SHA extensions, and BMI2.

The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage or managed disks for persistent data. It does not feature discrete GPUs, relying solely on CPU resources for compute tasks. In benchmark evaluations, memory throughput achieves 102.57 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB read blocks and 59.08 GB/sec for write operations, with cached small-block reads reaching 834.31 GB/sec. General multi-core processing delivers a Geekbench score of 10035.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 21180.44. In memory-dependent operations, it sustains 16.03 million Redis SET operations per second and handles 21.78 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

Cost efficiency is centered around memory density rather than raw multi-core compute throughput. Because the hardware dedicates 128.0 GB of RAM across 16 vCPUs, it avoids the expense of scaling compute core counts purely to acquire large memory capacity. The trade-off is the absence of local ephemeral NVMe storage, meaning all I/O workloads rely on remote storage throughput limits. The instance is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers, memory-heavy analytics pipelines, and multi-threaded compilation workloads.

It features 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores, paired with 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Cache provisions include 260 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512 and hardware cryptography. The instance includes no bundled local storage and no dedicated GPUs. Performance benchmarks show sustained uncached memory read bandwidth of 102.57 GB/sec, 16.03 million Redis SET operations per second, a Geekbench multi-core score of 10035.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 21180.44. By prioritizing memory allocation per core, the E16s_v5 delivers cost efficiency for RAM-intensive tasks without requiring higher core tiers. It is well-matched for large in-memory caches, relational database systems, and data analytics tasks requiring substantial memory headroom.
